# MicroDuck Movement Policy and Task Development Topic

This topic compiles materials related to reinforcement learning, motion control, physical simulation, task scheduling, and on-device deployment for MicroDuck / OpenDuck Mini V2. The directory is organized in the order of “first running the baseline, then understanding the code, and finally developing tasks,” making it suitable for following the learning process while gradually adding experimental records.

## Learning Path

1. First, examine [ basketball balance ](01-task-information/01-microduck-basketball-balance-reinforcement-learning/README.md) to understand the velocity command, 61-dimensional observation, 14-dimensional action, PPO, and contact rewards.
2. Then, look at [ browser physical perturbation ](01-task-information/02-mjswan-microduck-browser-physical-disturbance/README.md) to grasp the MuJoCo state, perturbation, recording, and visualization interfaces.
3. Move on to [ stilt walking ](01-task-information/03-microduck-stilt-walker-reinforcement-learning-reproduction/README.md) to learn about actuator parameters, shape curriculum, action smoothing, and sim-to-real constraints.
4. Study [ swinging rotation ](01-task-information/04-microduck-sway-rotation-reinforcement-learning-reproduction/README.md) and [ ball balance and FastSAC ](01-task-information/05-motrixlab-microduck-ball-balance-and-fastsac/README.md) to compare different tasks and algorithm interfaces.
5. Finally, proceed to [ ladder climbing ](01-task-information/06-microduck-tread-climbing-reinforcement-learning-guide/README.md) by examining the support curriculum, real rail contact, and landing state machine step by step.
6. When running or modifying code is required, enter [ executable code package ](02-executable-code/microduck-playground-stilts/README.md).
7. For viewing RDK X5, web demos, and multi-policy scheduling, go to [ side-mounted and web deployment ](01-task-information/07-rdk-on-side-and-web-deployment/README.md).
8. If checking operations according to the live broadcast sequence is needed, open [ Notebook learning entry point ](03-Notebook/README.md).

## Notebook Learning Line

The Notebook is recommended to run on an Ubuntu workstation. On Windows, Jupyter can only be accessed via a browser. In this way, MuJoCo, training code, and Python dependencies are all in the same environment. The Notebook then connects to sunrise@192.168.8.128 via SSH, using RDK X5 as an independent BPU inference endpoint. The Notebook includes built-in workstation information, SSH detection, ONNX contract verification, and HBM/BPU validation, eliminating the need for an additional layer of "Windows Notebook -> Ubuntu -> RDK" transition.

The ordinary ONNX model on the board cannot be directly used as a BPU model. It is necessary to generate an HBM using a compiler compatible with the RDK X5 SDK first. Currently, hrt_model_exec, hobot_dnn, and /dev/bpu have been verified on the board, but hb_mapper has not been installed yet; therefore, the Notebook can now complete the board connectivity and BPU operation authentication. For the actual BPU inference under the MicroDuck policy, the corresponding HBM files are still required.

## Current Status

| Task | Current Organization Status | Result Boundaries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Basketball Balance | Existing tutorials, videos, evaluation records, and local execution interfaces | Can serve as a public checkpoint for reproduction, but is not equivalent to the newly trained model |
| Browser Physical Disturbance | Existing browser demonstrations and recording scripts | Primarily focused on visualization and interaction verification; not a new policy training result |
| Stilt Walking | Existing replay, hardware materials, and training instructions for 25 cm/2 m | Used as a morphology course case study; need to distinguish between simulation replays and real robot safety verification |
| Swinging Rotation | Existing reproduction descriptions, ONNX files, and videos | Used for comparison tasks, export, and deployment interfaces |
| Ball Balance and FastSAC | Existing organized public methods and local reproduction materials | Need to judge based on the success criteria in their respective README files; do not consider smoke results as final outcomes |
| Ladder Climbing | Existing V1/V2/V3 scenarios, code, and failure replays | Currently cannot be described as “already stable at the top”; ladder climbing has not been successful, and the obstacle avoidance route still requires further inspection |
| RDK X5 / Web Deployment | Existing ONNX, TCP, web policy bridge, multi-duck scheduling, and local replay materials | Need to record model versions, observation dimensions, and edge hardware tests separately; do not consider web demonstrations as real robot results |

## Code Source and Boundaries

`02-可运行代码/microduck-playground-stilts/` It is from the local location.
`microduck-playground-stilts` The reproduction-ready lightweight snapshot generated from the working directory includes the current task code, as well as the added ramp surface, executor, evaluation, and testing materials. No copies are made `.venv/`Logs, training caches, checkpoints, and generated results; these files are large in size and tied to the local environment, and should not be directly submitted to the main repository.

Upstream project:

- [Vottivott/microduck-playground](https://github.com/Vottivott/microduck-playground)
- [pollen-robotics/microduck_rl](https://github.com/pollen-robotics/microduck_rl)

Modifications and experimental patches in the code package should continue to be labeled as "upstream code" or "local cleanup/experimental code". Do not refer to the experimental patches as official releases.

## Video Materials

To control the size of the main repository, only GIFs, keyframe images, and covers are submitted for the专题; the original MP4 files are not saved with the main branch. Each demonstration video corresponds to a `*_keyframes.jpg` located in the original `assets/` or `精选视频/` directory, which is used to quickly check the action stages and results. If continuous videos are needed, re-export them according to the commands in the task README, or use the public link provided in the README.

## Subsequent Logging Methods

For each new experiment, it is recommended to record at least: task name, code version, checkpoint, number of environments, number of training epochs, random seed, success status, video path, and current conclusion. For failed experiments, clearly write "Not completed" and the specific failure points, such as "failure at the foot of the ladder" or "no continuous shifting occurred". Do not keep only a seemingly normal segment.
